srishti: FYI seeing a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for RAG-longcontext after the kernel-selection commit from last week :eyes:

srishti: Quick numbers from canary: RAG workload (avg doc length ~3k tokens) hit_rate went from ~72% -> ~44%, end-to-end p95 generation latency jumped 120ms -> 310ms, token cost up ~1.8x.

anya: whoa, 44% is huge. is this just canary or also observed in dedicated nodes? :thinking:

srishti: Only in canary so far. Dedicated baseline still on old kernel; canary got the new attention kernel + updated batching heuristics.
\
jkramer: do we have a breakdown of misses by cause? eviction vs key-mismatch (normalization) vs mismatched keying for structured outputs?
\
srishti: quick dump from metrics service:
```
prefix_cache: {
  hit_rate: 0.44,
  keys_total: 234k,
  evictions_per_min: 3.2k,
  key_cardinality_bucket: { short_prefix: 60%, long_prefix: 30%, convo_meta: 10% }
}
# sample miss reason tags: [evicted, key_mismatch, not_cached_schema]
```

dave: two hypotheses: 1) kernel now favors a different batching/coalescing path that changes per-request tokenization/windowing -> cache key normalization diverges, 2) kernel changed the KV layout (aligned/packed) and our cache fingerprinting used memory offsets?

anya: kernel shouldn't touch high-level keying, but batching can change how we slice prefixes. did we change the prefix fingerprint (hash) anywhere in the runtime? commit?

jkramer: I grep'd the rollout diff: no explicit hash change, but `batch_coalesce()` now merges adjacent requests earlier which can collapse conversation fragments into different prefix boundaries. Could explain more evictions and key-mismatch.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary group `rk-canary-3` updated with `kernel-attn-v2` at 2026-11-02T09:12Z by jkramer.

dave: ok, two quick experiments to isolate:
- run microbench with identical tokenization but force old and new batching paths (toggle flag)
- run warmup prefetch for top-100 prefixes observed in 24h and compare hit-rate

srishti: microbench results (10k requests RAG-sim):
```
old-batching: hit_rate 0.71, p95 115ms
new-batching: hit_rate 0.45, p95 305ms
key_mismatch_tagging: new-batching shows +27% key_mismatch vs old
```

anya: yep that points to batching boundary changes. for structured outputs we delimit with `\n<sep>\n` and sometimes coalescing removes that sep into the body -> different prefix fingerprint.

jkramer: short term mitigation: revert the automatic coalesce for RAG-like routes (route config override) so we keep old boundary semantics. medium-term: make fingerprinting robust to adjacent coalescing by canonicalizing separators and convo metadata ordering.

dave: can we A/B toggle the coalesce flag per-route and run a canary? I can patch route config and run 6h canary.

infra-bot: rollout plan created: `coalesce-toggle` route-override -> 50% canary for `rk-canary-3` then 100% if metrics stable. See https://internal/release/issue/4582

srishti: also proposing a warmup strategy: prefetch top-N prefixes at pod startup (async, low priority) and keep a small reservoir of top-keys pinned in LRU to prevent immediate evictions during bursty RAG requests. We saw immediate hit-rate improvement in local sim: +18% when prefetching top-200 keys.

anya: that would add some startup IO but it's bounded. we should also add an offline job that computes canonicalized prefix fingerprints to compare old vs new over historical traces to find where canonicalization is different.

jkramer: action items:
- dave: roll `coalesce-toggle` canary (in 15m) and post results (first pass 6h)
- srishti: run offline prefix canonicalization diff and produce top-100 mismatches by frequency
- anya: prototype prefetch pinned-reservoir in runtime (configurable N) and measure memory IO impact

dave: got it, starting canary now. ping me if you want logs/metrics dashboards. :thumbsup:

srishti: thanks. if canary confirms this, we'll ship a targeted rollback of the batching coalesce for RAG routes and keep the kernel optimizations for other workloads.

anya: and follow-up: add a small unit test that asserts prefix -> fingerprint is stable across batching modes for canonicalized input.

srishti: +1. I'll open a follow-up RFC describing the canonicalization rules and the warmup/reservoir design.

dave: update after 6h: canary `coalesce-toggle=off` -> hit_rate back to ~70%, p95 back to ~125ms. posting graphs in #perf-dash in 10m.

jkramer: great, marking this as regression caused by batching coalescing interaction with prefix keying. we should avoid global coalesce defaults without route-level review.

infra-bot: incident-note: assigned `perf-regression-2026-11-02`, severity: low, owner: dave.

srishti: closing loop: once rollback is confirmed I'll coordinate a changelist that keeps the kernel attention perf gains but reworks the coalescing heuristics to be cache-aware.

anya: thanks everyone. saved us a lot of tokens. :coffee:
